narrative.overview: A replacement world for the retired portfolio identity. The page is one garment seen once, at one scale: a panelled black-and-off-white cloth field carries the team name and a player print, a woven tag carries the seven names and one-word roles, and a yellow care label carries the only Shop action. The category-default fan site is refused. Color lives in materials, not decoration; a single NAVI-yellow piping thread marks the seam, the active control, the selected tag row and the Shop tab.
keyCharacteristics: One panelled cloth field, one diagonal piping seam, one woven tag column.
Yellow is a stitch and a state signal, never a content field.
Heat-pressed condensed caps for identity; tiny tracked caps for the woven tag.
Squared 2px corners and dashed seam borders — garment hardware, not UI chrome.

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks the seam, identity and state only. If two large yellow regions compete for the same viewport, reduce all but the primary action.

rules.name: The Unbroken Print Rule
rules.body: A cutout that is loading or has failed never breaks the field — the swatch and a monogram hold the space.

dos: Do keep the cloth panels, diagonal piping and woven tag — remove them and the world disappears.
Do self-host Archivo, the player cutouts and every merchandise image; no hosted font stylesheet or hotlinks.
Do keep all facts to the verified roster, fixtures, awards and Season 18 statistics, each with a named source.
Do keep visible role vocabulary to one word: JUNGLE, EXP, MID, GOLD, ROAM.
Do route repeated values through the named tokens in :root.
donts: Don't invent jersey numbers, prices, products, seller URLs, testimonials or endorsements.
Don't present fan-made merchandise as officially endorsed — the border and badge are mandatory.
Don't replace the garment with a hero photograph over a card grid, or the piping with a second accent color.
Don't let a broken image glyph stand in for a missing portrait or product image; keep the designed fallback.
